
---
title: Technical prerequisites
--- 

Before we begin working with R, Python, and Quarto in Advanced Empirical Finance, please set up your computer so that you can run code from day one. No prior experience with programming or development tools is required — this guide walks you through everything step by step. Should you encounter any issues, please do not hesitate to contact your TAs or me for assistance. To facilitate collaboration, please ask me via the Absalon discussion board to make sure everyone can benefit from the solution.

## Prerequisites


### Install the required software

1.  Install [Positron (latest Version)](https://positron.posit.co/start.html). *Positron is the integrated development environment (IDE) we use. It supports R, Python, Git, and Quarto in one place. Install Positron using the default settings.*
2.  Register a free account on [GitHub](https://github.com/). *GitHub allows us to share course materials and collaborate.*
3.  Install [Git](https://git-scm.com/install/). *Git is the version control system we use to connect to GitHub.*
4.  Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) and [uvr](https://github.com/nbafrank/uvr). *uv installs Python and the Python packages of the course; uvr does the same for R. You don't install R or Python yourself.* Open a terminal and run the two lines for your system:

    macOS and Linux (Terminal):

    ```sh
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nbafrank/uvr/main/install.sh | sh
    ```

    Windows (PowerShell):

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nbafrank/uvr/main/install.ps1 | iex"
    ```

    Then close the terminal and open a new one, so it finds `uv` and `uvr`. If uv and uvr are already on your computer, for example from another course, update them instead with `uv self update` and `uvr upgrade`; the course needs uvr 0.4.8 or later.

### Set up your team repository

Every student works in a team, and a team of one is fine. Teams form during the dry run of the trading game, 25 January to 5 February. One person per team sends the team's name and the GitHub usernames of all members through the form on Absalon. We then create your team's private repository on GitHub, `aef27-<team>`: a copy of the [course repository](https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/course-repository) with the slides, the templates for the mandatory assignments, the R and Python environment and the `data` folder. GitHub emails each member an invitation; accept it within seven days.

5.  Clone your team repository in Positron:
     - Open the Source Control view {{< kbd Ctrl-Shift-G >}}. *If Git is not yet installed, the view shows how to install it.*
     - Click `Clone Repository` and paste the address of your team repository, with `<team>` replaced by your team's name:

       ```{.default}
       https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aef27-<team>.git
       ```

       Sign in to GitHub when your browser asks, and choose a local folder for the repository. Cloning means creating your own copy of a shared project on your computer, so you can work on it without affecting the original.
6. Open the cloned repository in Positron with `File` → `Open Folder`. Then open the Terminal (`Terminal` → `New Terminal`) and connect your repository to the course repository, so that new course material reaches you later:

    ```sh
    git remote add upstream https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/course-repository.git
    git config pull.rebase false
    ```

    How your team works with the repository and how course updates arrive: [collaboration with Git and GitHub](../additional-material/github-collaboration.qmd). The licensed data from Absalon go into the `data` folder; see [the exercises on financial data](introduction.qmd#financial-data).

### Install R, Python and the course packages

7. In the Terminal (not the Console) of Positron: because you opened your team repository in step 6, the Terminal starts in the repository's folder, the one that holds `uvr.toml` and `pyproject.toml`. Check with `pwd` (macOS and Linux) or `Get-Location` (Windows). Then run

    ```sh
    uvr r install 4.6.1
    uvr sync
    uv sync
    ```

    `uvr r install` installs R, `uvr sync` installs *all* R packages of the course, and `uv sync` installs Python and *all* Python packages of the course, including `aefsim`, the client for the [trading game](../trading-game/index.qmd). Everyone gets exactly the same package versions, because they are recorded in the repository (`uvr.lock` for R, `uv.lock` for Python). If Positron asks which R or Python to use, choose R 4.6.1 for R. For Python, choose the environment that `uv sync` just created in the `.venv` folder of your team repository: its path ends in `aef27-<team>/.venv`, not in a Python installed elsewhere on your computer.

    Adding a package works the same way in both: `uvr add tidymodels` for R, `uv add polars` for Python. To collaborate with your peers, commit the files `uvr.toml`, `uvr.lock`, `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`; your colleagues only have to run `uvr sync` and `uv sync` to replicate your exact package environment.

8. To verify that R is working correctly, click on `New/New File` and select `R file` to open a new R script in Positron and type 

    ```r
    library(tidyfinance)
    download_data(
            domain = "Stock Prices",
            symbols = "AAPL",
            start_date = "2000-01-01",
            end_date = "2023-12-31")
    ```

    Mark everything and press {{< kbd mac=Cmd-Enter win=Ctrl-Enter linux=Ctrl-Enter >}} to run the code. If everything is working correctly, you should see that you just downloaded financial data in the console. If you receive an error such as `there is no package called 'tidyfinance'`, Positron is not using the course's R: when R starts, the console should say `uvr: library linked (… packages)`. If it doesn't, choose R 4.6.1 with the interpreter icon on the top right, restart R (`Session` → `Restart R`), and run `uvr sync` in the Terminal again.

9. To verify that Python is working correctly, click on `New/New File` and select `Python file` to open a new Python script in Positron and type 

    ```python
    import tidyfinance as tf
    tf.download_data(
            domain="Stock Prices",
            symbols="AAPL",
            start_date="2000-01-01",
            end_date="2023-12-31")
    ```

    Mark everything and press {{< kbd mac=Cmd-Enter win=Ctrl-Enter linux=Ctrl-Enter >}} to run the code. If everything is working correctly, you should see that you just downloaded financial data in the console. If you receive an error, select the course's Python environment first: click on the interpreter icon on the top right and choose the one in the course repository's `.venv`.

### Render PDFs with TinyTeX

You hand in every mandatory assignment as a PDF that Quarto renders from your `.qmd` file. Quarto comes with Positron, but PDF output also needs LaTeX. Install TinyTeX, a small LaTeX distribution, once:

10. In Positron's Terminal, run:

    ```sh
    quarto install tinytex
    ```

11. Check the installation with `quarto check`. Under "Checking LaTeX", the output should name TinyTeX. If it says `Tex: (not detected)`, run the install command again, then restart Positron.

12. Test it: open `mandatory-assignments/MA_R_template.qmd` (or `MA_python_template.qmd`) from your team repository and click **Preview**. Positron shows the PDF in the Viewer.
